subject: verify-routine-wave-conflicts

## Approach

Add `test_end_to_end_wave_resolve` in `tests/test_wave_resolve.py`: a temporary repository and store, two task branches that edit different lines of one file, `cli.main(["wave","end",...])` stops on the conflict, the test edits the file to keep both changes, `cli.main(["wave","resolve",...])` exits 0 and the question is answered. subject: resolve-finish
body:
## Description

R3: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses unless every active acceptance of the incoming task passes on the merge commit.
R4: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses unless every active acceptance of each task already merged in the wave passes on the merge commit.
R6: A successful resolve commits the merge.
R7: A successful resolve records the check-runs at the merge commit.
R8: A successful resolve answers the blocking `merge:<task>` question.
R9: `orchestra wave end` continues with the remaining tasks after a successful resolve.

## Approach

Extend `resolve` in `orchestra/conductor/wave.py`. After the guards pass, stage the resolved files (`git add -u`) and build the merge commit without moving `HEAD`: `git write-tree`, then `git commit-tree -p HEAD -p <task-branch>`. Check that commit out in a temporary detached worktree and run the active acceptances of the incoming task and of every task already merged into the phase branch in this wave, through the same path `orchestra task land` uses. Record the check-runs at that commit. When any acceptance fails, remove the temporary worktree, change nothing else, leave the question open and refuse with the failing acceptance ids; the agent's edits and the merge state stay in the phase worktree. When all pass, fast-forward the phase worktree to that commit (`git merge --ff-only`), answer the question (`canon update --transition answered` through `Project`) and return success. `orchestra wave end` already skips branches that are ancestors of the phase branch, so a second run continues with the remaining tasks; add a test that proves it.

Tests in `tests/test_wave_resolve.py` with `-k` groups: `incoming_acceptance` (R3), `merged_acceptance` (R4), `commits_merge` (R6), `records_check_runs` (R7), `answers_question` (R8), `wave_end_continues` (R9). Write them first and see them fail.
title: Run both tasks' acceptances and finish the merge

subject: resolve-guards
body:
## Description

R1: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses while an unmerged path remains in the phase worktree.
R2: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses while a conflict marker remains in a tracked file.
R5: A refused resolve leaves the blocking `merge:<task>` question open.

## Approach

In `orchestra/conductor/wave.py` add `resolve(project, repo, phase, task)` and a `ResolveRefusal` result. It reads the open `merge:<task>` question for the phase effort (`_open_question`) and refuses when none is open. In the phase worktree it refuses while `git ls-files --unmerged` lists a path. It refuses while any tracked file holds a line that starts with `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` (`git grep -nE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)( |$)'`). With a clean tree it returns a `ready` result and changes nothing; `resolve-finish` adds the rest. Expose `orchestra wave resolve <phase> <task>` in `orchestra/cli.py` next to `wave start` and `wave end`. A refusal prints each reason to stderr and exits 1. The question stays open and no record is written.

Tests in `tests/test_wave_resolve.py` build a temporary repository with a conflict between two task branches and a temporary store (see `tests/test_task_worktrees.py`). Name them so these `-k` filters pick one group each: `unmerged` (R1), `marker` (R2), `question_open` (R5). Write them first and see them fail.
title: Add wave resolve with its refusal checks

subject: conflict-skills
body:
## Description

R10: `execute-phase` tells the agent to ask the user when the two tasks need competing behavior.
R11: `plan-phase` tells the planner to add a `depends_on` edge between tasks that must rewrite the same function.

## Approach

Edit `skills/execute-phase/SKILL.md` step 6 and its Do-not list, and `skills/execute-phase/references/mechanics.md`. Keep that `wave end` stops on a conflict and opens the blocking question. Add: the parent resolves a routine conflict, where both tasks keep their behavior, by editing the conflicted files in the phase worktree and running `orchestra wave resolve <phase-slug> <task-slug>`; when the two tasks need competing behavior, leave the question open and ask the user. Replace "resolve a merge conflict" in the Do-not list with "resolve a merge conflict by any path other than `orchestra wave resolve`". Edit `skills/plan-phase/SKILL.md` and its `task-shapes.md`: add a `depends_on` edge between tasks that must rewrite the same function, so the later task builds on the earlier one.

Tests in `tests/test_conflict_skills.py`: `competing_behavior` (R10) and `depends_on_same_function` (R11) read the skill text. Update any consistency test that pins the old Do-not wording.
title: Tell agents when to resolve and when to ask

subject: routine-wave-conflicts
body:
## Requirements

R1: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses while an unmerged path remains in the phase worktree.
R2: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses while a conflict marker remains in a tracked file.
R3: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses unless every active acceptance of the incoming task passes on the merge commit.
R4: `orchestra wave resolve` refuses unless every active acceptance of each task already merged in the wave passes on the merge commit.
R5: A refused resolve leaves the blocking `merge:<task>` question open.
R6: A successful resolve commits the merge.
R7: A successful resolve records the check-runs at the merge commit.
R8: A successful resolve answers the blocking `merge:<task>` question.
R9: `orchestra wave end` continues with the remaining tasks after a successful resolve.
R10: `execute-phase` tells the agent to ask the user when the two tasks need competing behavior.
R11: `plan-phase` tells the planner to add a `depends_on` edge between tasks that must rewrite the same function.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test stages a conflict between two tasks that edit different lines of one file, resolves it, and sees the question answered.
- A test resolves with a marker left and sees a refusal.
- A test resolves a merge that breaks one task's acceptance and sees a refusal with the question open.
- A skill consistency test finds R10 and R11 text.

## Constraints

- Only the parent session writes records and runs `orchestra wave resolve`.
- `orchestra wave end` still never resolves a conflict on its own.
- No rebase of a task branch.

## Non-goals

- Automatic conflict resolution inside `wave end`.
- Detecting same-function overlap by static analysis at plan time.
- Resolving conflicts between phase branches or against `main`.

## Invariants

- A task branch whose checks did not pass is never merged.
- The phase worktree is the only integration checkout.
- A `done` task never reopens.

## Assumptions

- The agent that edits the conflicted files runs in the phase worktree.
- A task's acceptances are runnable at the merge commit in the phase worktree.
